name: Truth Tables of Compound Statements
problem:
Consider the following statement:

$$
A \land (B\lor A)
$$

 

We can use a truth table to calculate the truth values of this statement given all possible permutations of the truth values of $A$ and $B.$

First, we complete a truth table for the part in parentheses, $B \lor A.$  The statement $B \lor A$ is true if either $A$ is true, $B$ is true, or both $A$ and $B$ are true.

| $\,A\,$ | $\,B\,$ | $\,B \lor A\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $\textrm T$ | $\textrm T$ | $\textrm T$ |
| $\textrm T$ | $\textrm F$ | $\textrm T$ |
| $\textrm F$ | $\textrm T$ | $\textrm T$ |
| $\textrm F$ | $\textrm F$ | $\textrm F$ |

Next, we add a new column for $A \land (B\lor A).$ 

| $\,A\,$ | $\,B\,$ | $\,B \lor A\,$ | $\,A \land (B \lor A)\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\textrm T$ | $\textrm T$ | $\textrm T$ |  |
| $\textrm T$ | $\textrm F$ | $\textrm T$ |  |
| $\textrm F$ | $\textrm T$ | $\textrm T$ |  |
| $\textrm F$ | $\textrm F$ | $\textrm F$ |  |

To fill in the rows, we consider the truth values of $A$ and $(B\lor A)$ and use this to determine the truth value of $A \land (B\lor A)$ in each case.

- Consider the first row. Since $A$ is true and $(B\lor A)$ is true, their conjunction $A \land (B\lor A)$ is *true*:

| $\,A\,$ | $\,B\,$ | $\,B \lor A\,$ | $\,A \land (B \lor A)\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}\textrm T}$ | $\textrm T$ | $\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}\textrm T}$ | $\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}\textrm T}$ |
| $\textrm T$ | $\textrm F$ | $\textrm T$ |  |
| $\textrm F$ | $\textrm T$ | $\textrm T$ |  |
| $\textrm F$ | $\textrm F$ | $\textrm F$ |  |

- Next, consider the second row. Since $A$ is true and $(B\lor A)$ is true, their conjunction $A \land (B\lor A)$ is *true*:

| $\,A\,$ | $\,B\,$ | $\,B \lor A\,$ | $\,A \land (B \lor A)\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\textrm T$ | $\textrm T$ | $\textrm T$ | $\textrm T$ |
| $\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}\textrm T}$ | $\textrm F$ | $\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}\textrm T}$ | $\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}\textrm T}$ |
| $\textrm F$ | $\textrm T$ | $\textrm T$ |  |
| $\textrm F$ | $\textrm F$ | $\textrm F$ |  |

- Now, consider the third row. Since $A$ is false and $(B\lor A)$ is true, their conjunction $A \land (B\lor A)$ is *false*:

| $\,A\,$ | $\,B\,$ | $\,B \lor A\,$ | $\,A \land (B \lor A)\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\textrm T$ | $\textrm T$ | $\textrm T$ | $\textrm T$ |
| $\textrm T$ | $\textrm F$ | $\textrm T$ | $\textrm T$ |
| $\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}\textrm F}$ | $\textrm T$ | $\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}\textrm T}$ | $\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}\textrm F}$ |
| $\textrm F$ | $\textrm F$ | $\textrm F$ |  |

- Finally, consider the fourth row. Since $A$ is false and $(B\lor A)$ is false, their conjunction $A \land (B\lor A)$ is *false*:

| $\,A\,$ | $\,B\,$ | $\,B \lor A\,$ | $\,A \land (B \lor A)\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\textrm T$ | $\textrm T$ | $\textrm T$ | $\textrm T$ |
| $\textrm T$ | $\textrm F$ | $\textrm T$ | $\textrm T$ |
| $\textrm F$ | $\textrm T$ | $\textrm T$ | $\textrm F$ |
| $\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}\textrm F}$ | $\textrm F$ | $\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}\textrm F}$ | $\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}\textrm F}$ |

The completed truth table is shown below:

| $\,A\,$ | $\,B\,$ | $\,B \lor A\,$ | $\,A \land (B \lor A)\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\textrm T$ | $\textrm T$ | $\textrm T$ | $\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}\textrm T}$ |
| $\textrm T$ | $\textrm F$ | $\textrm T$ | $\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}\textrm T}$ |
| $\textrm F$ | $\textrm T$ | $\textrm T$ | $\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}\textrm F}$ |
| $\textrm F$ | $\textrm F$ | $\textrm F$ | $\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}\textrm F}$ |
